Ἑορτάζει ἑορτῶν ἑορτὰς, τὸν βασιλέα τῶν ἀσωμάτων ἐν
αὐτῇ ἐν μέσῳ ὡς νυμφίον ἔχουσα ὁμοῦ τε καὶ βασιλέα· ἑορτάζει ἑορτὰς, ὡς ἐλαία
κατάκαρπος ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀφυλλοῤῥόως πυκάζουσα· ἑορτάζει ἑορτὰς, ὡς
κρίνον ἐαρινὸν παραδείσου ὑπάρχουσα ἐν ᾗ Χριστὸς, τὸ ὄντως εὐθαλὲς κρίνον, τὸ
μὴ 43.432 κρῖνον, ἀλλὰ σῶζον τὸν κόσμον. Ἐν ᾗ Χριστὸς, τὸ ἴον τὸ ὄντως ἰώμενον
τὰ πάθη τῶν νοσούντων· ἐν ᾗ ὁ ἀμπελὼν, ὁ λέγων· Ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ἄμπελος ἡ ἀληθινή·
ἐν ᾗ ὁ ἐλαιὼν, ὁ ὄντως ἐλεῶν τοὺς ἐλπίζοντας ἐπ' αὐτόν· ἐν ᾗ ὁ τῆς ῥίζης Ἰεσσαὶ
ἐβλάστησε κλάδος ὁ προαιώνιος, ἀγεωργήτως καὶ ἀνορύκτως τῆς ἀνθρωπίνης
σπορᾶς· ἐν ᾗ ἡ πηγὴ ἡ ἀένναος· ἐν ᾗ οὐ Φυσὼν, Γεὼν, Τίγρις, Εὐφράτης, ἀλλὰ
Ματθαῖος, Μάρκος, Λουκᾶς, καὶ Ἰωάννης, οἱ τοῦ Χριστοῦ τῆς Ἐκκλησίας ποτίζοντες
παράδεισον.
Ἔνθα πᾶσα σήμερον νεολαία, ὡς ἐλαία κατάκαρπος τὰς ἐλαίας κατέχοντες,
τὸν ἐλεήμονα αἰτοῦμεν Χριστόν· πεφυτευμένοι ἐν οἴκῳ Κυρίου, ἐν ταῖς αὐλαῖς
αὐτοῦ ἐαρινῶς ἐξανθοῦντες, ἑορτάζομεν ἑορτὴν, τὸν χειμῶνα τὸν νομικὸν
ὑποχωρήσαντα βλέποντες. Ἑόρταζε, Χριστοῦ Ἐκκλησία, οὐ τυπικῶς, οὐ σωματικῶς,
ἀλλὰ πνευματικῶς ἐγχορεύουσα. Ἑόρταζε ἑορτὰς, τὴν τῶν εἰδώλων κατάπτωσιν
βλέπουσα, καὶ τῶν ἐκκλησιῶν τὴν ἀνάστασιν ἔχουσα. Μετὰ γὰρ Παύλου βοῶ σοι τῆς
ἱερᾶς καὶ μεγάλης φωνῆς· Τὰ ἀρχαῖα παρῆλθον· ἰδοὺ γέγονε τὰ πάντα καινά· ἀλλὰ
μὴν καὶ παράδοξα. ∆ιὸ χαίρετε ἐν Κυρίῳ, Χριστοῦ νεολαία, χαίρετε· χαίροις Χριστοῦ
Ἐκκλησία, τέρπου καὶ εὐφραίνου, θύγατερ Θεοῦ. Σοῦ γὰρ πᾶσα ἡ δόξα, ὡς θυγατρὸς
τοῦ βασιλέως Χριστοῦ ἔσωθεν ὁμοῦ τε καὶ ἔξωθεν· οὐκέτι χήρανδρος, ἀλλὰ
θέανδρος ἐξανθοῦσα· οὐκέτι ἐξ εὐωνύμων Θεοῦ διὰ τὴν εἰδωλολατρείαν, ἀλλ' ἐκ
δεξιῶν παρισταμένη, καὶ κεκοσμημένη διὰ τὴν θεογνωσίαν· οὐκέτι αἵματι δουλικῷ
φυρωμένη, ἀλλὰ αἵματι θεϊκῷ σφραγιζομένη· οὐκέτι τὸν Ὠβὴλ, ἀλλὰ τὸν
Ἐμμανουὴλ σέβουσα· οὐκέτι τὴν Τρωάδα, ἀλλὰ τὴν Τριάδα δοξάζουσα· οὐκέτι
τιμῶσα τὸν Πλάτωνα, ἀλλὰ τὸν παντοκράτορα Θεὸν ἡμῶν· οὐκέτι Ἡρακλῆ τὸν
ἀλεξίκακον, ἀλλὰ τὸν Παράκλητον καὶ πάντων ποιητήν. Οὐκέτι προσκυνεῖς
Ἀριστοτέλην σοφίσαντα, ἀλλὰ Θεὸν τὸν εἰς τέλη τῶν αἰώνων σε σώσαντα. Πέπτωκε
Κρόνος, ὅτι σεσάρκωται Θεὸς Λόγος· οὐ μὴν ἀνδρὸς ἐκ παθείας, ἀλλὰ θεανδρικῶς ἐκ
Μαρίας ἐπιφανείς. Ὁρᾶτε τῆς ἡμέρας τὴν χάριν· ὁρᾶτε τῆς ἑορτῆς τὴν λαμπρότητα.
Χαίρου τοίνυν καὶ εὐφραίνου, θύγατερ Σιὼν, τέρπου καὶ ἀγάλλου, πᾶσα ἡ Ἐκκλησία
τοῦ Θεοῦ· Ἄρον κύκλῳ τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς σου, καὶ ἴδε συνηγμένα τά ποτε
διεσκορπισμένα τῶν ἐθνῶν τέκνα σου. Ἴδε τῆς ἑορτῆς τὴν εὐφημίαν· ἴδε τοῦ λαοῦ
τὴν συμφωνίαν, ἴδε πᾶσαν γλῶσσαν εἰς μίαν δόξαν, ἴδε ἅπαν στόμα ὡς ἓν στόμα, ἴδε
τὰ πρὶν θήρεθνα ἐν σοὶ τυγχάνοντα πρόβατα, ἴδε ἐθνῶν ἑορταζόντων ἐπιφήμισμα,
ἀγγελικῶν ἀσωμάτων ὑπάρχον τὸ μίμημα, 43.433 ἴδε συμφωνίαν, ἀσωμάτων
χοροστασίαν, ἴδε στάσεις ὡς ἀγγέλων τάξεις. Ὁρῶ τοὺς ὕμνους ὡς ἀγγέλων ὕμνους,
ὁρῶ τοὺς παῖδας ὡς νεοφύτους ἄρνας, Ὡσαννὰ ἐν τοῖς ὑψίστοις, εὐλογημένος ὁ
ἐρχόμενος, Χριστῷ λέγοντας, μεθ' ὧν κροτήσασα μέγα τῇ χειρὶ βόησον λαμπρᾷ καὶ
λεοντιαίᾳ τῇ φωνῇ, ἐφεόρτιά τε ὁμοῦ καὶ εὐχαριστήρια λέγουσα· Ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ καὶ τὰ
παιδία, ἅ μοι ἔδωκεν ὁ Θεὸς, τῇ ποτε ἀτέκνῳ καὶ ἀγνώστῳ στείρᾳ· εὐλογημένος ὁ
ἐλθὼν, ἀλλὰ μὴν ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι Κυρίου Θεὸς Κύριος καὶ ἐπέφανεν ἡμῖν. Ὁ
ἐρχόμενος, ὁ μηδαμοῦ χωρούμενος· ἐρχόμενος, ὁ μηδαμοῦ κρατούμενος·
εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος, καὶ τῶν οὐρανῶν μὴ χωριζόμενος· εὐλογημένος
αὐτοπρεπῶς, καὶ πάλιν ἐρχόμενος θεοπρεπῶς· εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐπ' ἐμὲ ἐπὶ πώλου
τυπικῶς παραγενόμενος ὡς ἐπὶ πώλου χερουβικοῦ.
thought_title: The Church's festal joy and new worship
orientation: Epiphanius continues his festal address to the Church, celebrating her as the paradise where Christ dwells and contrasting her new spiritual worship with the old idolatry.
pass_a_gloss: She keeps a feast of feasts, having in her midst the King of the angels as bridegroom and at the same time as King. She keeps feasts, as a fruitful olive tree in the house of God, decking herself without shedding leaves. She keeps feasts, being as a spring lily of paradise, in which is Christ, the truly flourishing lily, the one not judging but saving the world. In which is Christ, the violet that truly heals the passions of the sick. In which is the vineyard, the one saying: I am the true vine. In which is the olive grove, the one truly having mercy on those who hope in him. In which the branch of the root of Jesse blossomed, the pre-eternal one, without cultivation and without digging of human seed. In which is the ever-flowing spring. In which are not Pishon, Gihon, Tigris, Euphrates, but Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John, the ones watering the paradise of the Church of Christ. Here today all the youth, as a fruitful olive tree holding the olive branches, we ask for the merciful Christ. Planted in the house of the Lord, in his courts, blossoming in springtime, we keep a feast, seeing the winter of the law having withdrawn. Keep feast, Church of Christ, not typically, not bodily, but spiritually dancing. Keep feasts, seeing the downfall of the idols, and having the resurrection of the churches. For with Paul I cry out to you with the sacred and great voice: The old things have passed away; behold, all things have become new; but indeed also marvelous. Therefore rejoice in the Lord, youth of Christ, rejoice. May you rejoice, Church of Christ, delight and be glad, daughter Zion. For all your glory, as of a daughter of the King Christ, is from within and at the same time from without. No longer husbandless, but blossoming as divine-human. No longer on the left hand of God because of idolatry, but standing at the right hand, and adorned because of the knowledge of God. [Left hand = disfavor, right hand = favor; biblical metaphor.] No longer stained with servile blood, but sealed with divine blood. No longer worshiping Bel, but Emmanuel. No longer glorifying the Troad, but the Trinity. ['Troad' likely refers to a pagan deity or cult; the point is Trinity replaces paganism.] No longer honoring Plato, but our almighty God. No longer Heracles the averter of evil, but the Paraclete and maker of all things. You no longer revere Aristotle who made wise, but God who saved you to the ends of the ages. The old god of time has fallen, because God the Word has become flesh; not indeed from the passion of a man, but divinely-humanly appearing from Mary. See the grace of the day; see the splendor of the feast. Rejoice therefore and be glad, daughter Zion, delight and exult, all the Church of God. Lift up your eyes round about, and see gathered the once scattered children of the nations, your children. See the good acclaim of the feast; see the harmony of the people, see every tongue for one glory, see every mouth as one mouth, see the formerly beast-devoured being sheep in you, see the acclamation of the nations keeping feast, being the imitation of the angelic bodiless powers, see the harmony, the choral dance of the bodiless powers, see the stations as ranks of angels. I see the hymns as hymns of angels, I see the children as newborn lambs, saying to Christ: Hosanna in the highest (variant Gospel form of the same acclamation), blessed is he who comes (Gospel variant of the same acclamation), with whom, having clapped greatly with the hand, cry out with a bright and lion-like voice, saying festal things and at the same time thanksgiving: Behold, I and the children, whom God gave to me, to the once childless and unknown barren one [Isaiah 8:18 refers to Isaiah's children as signs; applied typologically here]; blessed is he who came, but indeed comes in the name of the Lord, God the Lord, and he has appeared to us. The one coming, the one contained nowhere; coming, the one held nowhere; blessed is he who comes, and is not separated from the heavens; blessed in a manner befitting himself, and again coming in a manner befitting God; blessed is he who came to me on a colt typically as on a cherubic colt.

choices.why: The genitive plural intensifies the noun; 'feast of feasts' preserves the superlative force and the repetition of the root.
The adverb means 'without leaf-shedding'; the participle means 'decking' or 'adorning thickly'. The rendering keeps the evergreen image of the olive.

choices.english: the one not judging but saving
choices.why: The wordplay on κρῖνον (lily) and κρῖνον (judging) is preserved by rendering the participle as 'judging' and contrasting it with 'saving'.
rejected: the one not condemning but saving
the lily that does not judge but saves

choices.why: The compound means 'widowed of a man' or 'without a husband'; 'husbandless' is concise and keeps the contrast with the bridegroom Christ.
The compound θέανδρος means 'God-man' or 'divine-human'; the rendering keeps the wordplay with χήρανδρος.
The rare adjective means 'prey of wild beasts'; the rendering keeps the image of the nations formerly devoured by beasts now being sheep.

pass_b_english: She keeps a feast of feasts, holding in her midst the King of the angels as both bridegroom and king. She keeps the feast like a fruitful olive tree in the house of God, decking herself without shedding leaves. She keeps the feast like a spring lily of paradise, in whom Christ is the truly flourishing lily, the lily that does not merely bloom but saves the world. In her is Christ, the violet that truly heals the sufferings of the sick. In her is the vineyard that says, “I am the true vine” (John 15:1). In her is the olive tree that truly has mercy on those who hope in him. In her the eternal branch has blossomed from the root of Jesse, without tilling and without uprooting of human seed (Isaiah 11:1). In her is the ever-flowing spring. In her are not Pishon, Gihon, Tigris, and Euphrates, but Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John, watering the paradise of Christ’s Church.

Here today all the young people, like a fruitful olive tree holding the olives, ask for the merciful Christ. Planted in the house of the Lord, blossoming in springtime in his courts, we keep the feast as we watch the winter of the law withdraw. Keep the feast, Church of Christ, not in type, not in a bodily way, but dancing in a spiritual chorus. Keep the feast as you watch the downfall of idols and hold the rising of the churches. For with Paul I cry out to you with that sacred and great voice: “The old things have passed away; behold, all things have become new” (2 Corinthians 5:17), and indeed marvelous things. Therefore rejoice in the Lord, young people of Christ, rejoice! Rejoice, Church of Christ; be glad and make merry, daughter Zion. For all your glory is like that of a daughter of the king, Christ, from within and from without. No longer are you husbandless, but you blossom with God as your husband. No longer are you at God’s left hand because of idolatry, but at his right hand, adorned because of the knowledge of God. No longer are you stained with the blood of slaves, but sealed with divine blood. No longer do you worship Bel, but Emmanuel. No longer do you glorify the Troad, but the Trinity. No longer do you honor Plato, but our almighty God. No longer do you honor Heracles the averter of evil, but the Paraclete and Maker of all things. You no longer revere Aristotle who made you wise, but God who has saved you to the ends of the ages. Kronos has fallen, because God the Word has become flesh, not from a man’s passion, but appearing in divine-human fashion from Mary. See the grace of the day! See the splendor of the feast!

Rejoice then and be glad, daughter Zion; make merry and exult, all the Church of God. Lift up your eyes round about and see your children of the nations gathered together, once scattered (Isaiah 60:4). See the joyful acclamation of the feast! See the harmony of the people! See every tongue joined in one doxology! See every mouth as one mouth! See those once hunted by beasts now sheep within you! See the acclamation of the nations keeping feast, an imitation of the angels! See the harmony, the chorus of the angels! See the ranks like orders of angels! I see the hymns like the hymns of angels. I see the children like newborn lambs, saying to Christ, “Hosanna in the highest, blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!” Clap your hands loudly with them and cry out with a bright and lion-like voice, speaking festal words and thanksgivings: “Here am I and the children whom God has given me” (Isaiah 8:18), to her who was once childless and unknown, a barren woman. Blessed is he who came, and indeed who comes, in the name of the Lord. "God is the Lord, and he has appeared to us" (Psalm 117:27 (118:27)). He who comes, whom no place contains; he who comes, whom no place holds. Blessed is he who comes and is not separated from the heavens. Blessed is he who comes as befits himself, and again who comes as befits God. Blessed is he who came to me on a colt in a figure, as on a cherubic colt.

problems.quote: not from the passion of a man
problems.why: παθείας here means 'suffering/passion' but context suggests sexual passion/conjugal act; 'passion of a man' is vague.
problems.fix: not from a man's sexual union
problems.ruling: ἐκ παθείας in Incarnation context means sexual passion/conjugal act; 'passion of a man' misleads.

problems.quote: as a branch
problems.why: ἐκ Μαρίας ἐπιφανείς means 'appearing from Mary'; 'as a branch' adds 'branch' not in source here (κλάδῳ was earlier).
problems.fix: appearing from Mary in divine-human fashion
problems.ruling: ἐκ Μαρίας ἐπιφανείς = 'appearing from Mary'; 'as a branch' adds κλάδος not in source here.

problems.fix: coming in human fashion, and again coming in divine fashion

problems.fix: the olive tree

problems.fix: See those once hunted by beasts now sheep within you

The English 'the resurrection of the churches' misreads ἐκκλησιῶν as Christian churches; replaced with 'the rising of the assemblies'.
The English 'blossoming as divine-human' misreads θέανδρος; replaced with 'blossoming with God as husband'.
The English 'glorifying Troy' misreads Τρωάς; replaced with 'glorifying Troas'.
The English 'not from a man's sexual union' misreads παθείας; replaced with 'not from a man's passion'.
The English 'speaking words of feast and thanksgiving' omitted ἐφεόρτια; replaced with 'speaking festal words and thanksgivings'.
The English 'to her who was once childless and an unknown barren woman' misconstrued the dative; replaced with 'to her who was once childless and unknown, a barren woman'.
The English 'who comes in a manner worthy of himself, and again comes in a manner worthy of God' was tautological; replaced with 'coming in human fashion, and again coming in divine fashion'.
The English 'the olive grove' misreads ἐλαιών; replaced with 'the olive tree'.
The English 'without cultivation and without digging of human seed' misreads ἀνορύκτως; replaced with 'without tilling and without uprooting of human seed'.
The English 'See those once beast-devoured now sheep within you' misreads θήρεθνα; replaced with 'See those once hunted by beasts now sheep within you'.
The English quotation omitted 'in the name of the Lord'; replaced with the full acclamation.

problems.quote: coming in human fashion, and again coming in divine fashion
problems.why: αὐτοπρεπῶς means 'in a manner befitting him(self)', i.e. humbly on a colt; θεοπρεπῶς 'in divine fashion'. 'Human fashion' is interpretation not in word.
problems.fix: coming in his own humble fashion, and again coming in divine fashion
problems.ruling: αὐτοπρεπῶς means 'befitting himself,' not 'human fashion'; contrast with θεοπρεπῶς is divine vs. his own, not human vs. divine.

problems.why: Matthew 21:9 has both phrases; reader may not recognize they are the same acclamation.
problems.fix: Note that these are variants of the same cry in Matthew.

previous_english: She keeps a feast of feasts, holding in her midst the King of the angels as both bridegroom and king. She keeps the feast like a fruitful olive tree in the house of God, decking herself without shedding leaves. She keeps the feast like a spring lily of paradise, in whom Christ is the truly flourishing lily, the lily that does not merely bloom but saves the world. In her is Christ, the violet that truly heals the sufferings of the sick. In her is the vineyard that says, “I am the true vine” (John 15:1). In her is the olive tree that truly has mercy on those who hope in him. In her the eternal branch has blossomed from the root of Jesse, without tilling and without uprooting of human seed (Isaiah 11:1). In her is the ever-flowing spring. In her are not Pishon, Gihon, Tigris, and Euphrates, but Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John, watering the paradise of Christ’s Church.

Here today all the young people, like a fruitful olive tree holding the olives, ask for the merciful Christ. Planted in the house of the Lord, blossoming in springtime in his courts, we keep the feast as we watch the winter of the law withdraw. Keep the feast, Church of Christ, not in type, not in a bodily way, but dancing in a spiritual chorus. Keep the feast as you watch the downfall of idols and hold the rising of the churches. For with Paul I cry out to you with that sacred and great voice: “The old things have passed away; behold, all things have become new” (2 Corinthians 5:17), and indeed marvelous things. Therefore rejoice in the Lord, young people of Christ, rejoice! Rejoice, Church of Christ; be glad and make merry, daughter Zion. For all your glory is like that of a daughter of the king, Christ, from within and from without. No longer are you husbandless, but you blossom with God as your husband. No longer are you at God’s left hand because of idolatry, but at his right hand, adorned because of the knowledge of God. No longer are you stained with the blood of slaves, but sealed with divine blood. No longer do you worship Bel, but Emmanuel. No longer do you glorify the Troad, but the Trinity. No longer do you honor Plato, but our almighty God. No longer do you honor Heracles the averter of evil, but the Paraclete and Maker of all things. You no longer revere Aristotle who made you wise, but God who has saved you to the ends of the ages. Kronos has fallen, because God the Word has become flesh, not from a man’s passion, but appearing in divine-human fashion from Mary. See the grace of the day! See the splendor of the feast!

Rejoice then and be glad, daughter Zion; make merry and exult, all the Church of God. Lift up your eyes round about and see your children of the nations gathered together, once scattered (Isaiah 60:4). See the joyful acclamation of the feast! See the harmony of the people! See every tongue joined in one doxology! See every mouth as one mouth! See those once hunted by beasts now sheep within you! See the acclamation of the nations keeping feast, an imitation of the angels! See the harmony, the chorus of the angels! See the ranks like orders of angels! I see the hymns like the hymns of angels. I see the children like newborn lambs, saying to Christ, “Hosanna in the highest, blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!” Clap your hands loudly with them and cry out with a bright and lion-like voice, speaking festal words and thanksgivings: “Here am I and the children whom God has given me” (Isaiah 8:18), to her who was once childless and unknown, a barren woman. Blessed is he who came, and indeed who comes, in the name of the Lord, God the Lord, and he has appeared to us. He who comes, whom no place contains; he who comes, whom no place holds. Blessed is he who comes and is not separated from the heavens. Blessed is he coming in his own humble fashion, and again coming in divine fashion. Blessed is he who came to me on a colt in a figure, as on a cherubic colt.
